request: Goal: Correct workflow retro code-target classification for tracked implementation paths. Scope: Determine code eligibility from the retro target project's configured or bounded tracked source roots; support tracked src/flow/... and src/lib/... candidates; preserve existing lib/, commands/, hooks/, and root-config eligibility; retain fail-closed handling for unsafe, external, untracked, and excessive targets. Out of Scope: Changing retro candidate safety constraints or adding repository-specific rules. Description: Fix the plugin-layout bias so in-project candidates with tracked src implementation files are displayed and can be added with retro --add. Cover the behavior with unit/CLI tests and update workflow skill or CLI documentation.

R2: tests, specs, docs, fixtures, skills, and agent paths are excluded from production src eligibility. R3: legacy lib/, commands/, hooks/, plugin.json, and config paths remain eligible. R4: scope, empty/over-limit, unsafe, untracked, and tracked-file-cap prerequisites fail closed before eligibility. R5: display and --add share the evaluation map; the command context now maps clients.board to the workflow board client and retro results preserve the original sourceTitle. R6: tracked non-production paths remain non-code even with a src root. R8: source-root detection is cached per display/add evaluation and the cached workflow flow includes src candidates. T-1 through T-4 and the corrected command invocation were inspected; the spec-local test passes 8/8.
